newsitem.title: UK: Kvaerner to restructure hydro business.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner to restructure hydro business.

text.p: Norway's Kvaerner said on Monday that it was planning to restructure its hydro power business at a cost of $30 million.
As part of the reorganisation, most production of its hydro power equipment in the Nordic region would be concentrated at the Kvaerner Energy works in Sorumsand, outside Oslo.
Kvaerner said the move would strengthen Norwegian expertise in hydropower technology and enhance the firm's competitiveness in international markets.
One direct consequence of the current plan would be the transfer of production of hydro-mechanical equipment from Kvaerner Energy's Lodalen works in Oslo to Sorumsand.

"After being expanded and upgraded to specialise in manufacturing high-tech products, the Sorumsand works would become Kvaerner's principle Nordic facility for hydro-mechanical equipment," the group said.
Kvaerner said it also plans to construct a modern research and development centre in north of Oslo with engineering, project organisations and associated operations.

"We are not proposing changes which will end our traditional activities in Lodalen with a easy heart, but we must adapt to trends in this sector and this market," Kvaerner's president and CEO Erik Tonseth said.
The team of thermal power specialists currently based in Lodalen would move to the group's new technology centre at Lysaker outside Oslo.
Production of subsea installations for oil and gas production will be relocated from Lodalen to the Kvaerner Eureka works at Transby, west of Oslo.
The property in Lodalen would be sold offered for sale.
"Kvaerner Energy currently has about 900 employees in Norway. The planned changes will reduce this workforce by approximately 20-25 percent," the group said.
